report.verdict: Customer success work with a strong renewal result, hidden behind a job-search headline and an in-house title.
write_up: You managed mid-market accounts for a shipping software company, ran renewals and wrote an onboarding guide. A recruiter has enough here to consider messaging, but has to look past a headline about your search and an unfamiliar job title to find the work.

The Parcelwise renewal line is the model: it names the conversations you ran and the 91% of accounts by revenue renewed in 2025. That result is already on your profile, ready to carry into your About section.

Start with the headline and About so they introduce your customer success work, then make the Parcelwise title easier to understand. Add the kinds of tickets you handled in the earlier support job. Together, those changes give someone hiring for customer success a clearer reason to write.

cards.line: Open to work | Seeking new opportunities in Customer Success
cards.cannot_tell: Your headline leads with the search, not the work. You managed mid-market accounts and renewals for a shipping software company. Put that work first.
cards.example: Customer Success | Mid-market accounts | Shipping software
cards.question: What kind of shipping software did your accounts use?

cards.line: Customer success professional currently seeking my next opportunity. Open to remote roles. Please reach out if you think I could be a fit for your team.
cards.cannot_tell: This asks a recruiter to reach out before showing them why. Your Parcelwise job already has the account book, renewal result and onboarding guide to open with.
cards.example: I managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts for a shipping software company. I ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations and renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025. I wrote the onboarding guide new accounts get in their first week.
cards.question: What kind of customer success role are you seeking next?

cards.where: Parcelwise, Customer Happiness Hero II title
cards.cannot_tell: This title means something at Parcelwise, but it doesn't name the account and renewal work you describe. Put the standard job name alongside it once you've chosen the one that fits.
cards.example: Customer Happiness Hero II | [standard job title]
cards.question: At another company, would this job be called Customer Success Manager or Account Manager, or something else?

cards.where: Parcelwise, Customer Happiness Hero II description
cards.line: Ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations; renewed 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025.
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this line as the model. It names the work and the renewal result, with the measure and year attached.
Zendesk names the tool, but the tickets could cover almost anything. The types of issues and who sent them would show what your support work involved.
cards.example: Answered support tickets in Zendesk about [types of issues] for [who submitted tickets].
cards.question: What kinds of issues did you answer tickets about, and who sent them?

cards.cannot_tell: Problem Solving is a trait, not the customer success work a recruiter can filter for. Your job description already names quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations.
cards.example: Zendesk | quarterly business reviews | renewal conversations
cards.question: Which skills did you use to run reviews and renewal conversations?

fit.why: Your headline names Customer Success, and your Parcelwise work covers accounts, reviews, renewals and onboarding.
fit.level: mid-level, managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts
fit.note: 'Customer Success' is in your headline. 'Mid-market accounts' and 'quarterly business reviews' are in your Parcelwise description, while 'Zendesk' is in your top skills and support job. Customer health and churn are common customer success terms that aren't on your profile; add them only if they describe your work. Move mid-market accounts into your headline.
